records.text: The administration did not voluntarily release the Epstein files; Congress forced the release with a veto-proof majority.
records.speaker: Jared Moskowitz

appearances.snippet: You guys didn't release the files. ... You were forced by Congress. ... Every member of the House except one and the entire Senate. ... The reason the president signed it is because it was a veto-proof majority. ... and yet the entire House but one member and the whole Senate forced the administration to release the files.

verification.notes: Congress's official action record shows the Epstein Files Transparency Act passed the House 427-1 and the Senate by unanimous consent, margins sufficient to override a veto. The White House records that President Trump signed H.R. 4405 into law.

sources.title: H.R. 4405 All Actions
sources.relevance: Official legislative history records the 427-1 House vote and Senate unanimous consent.

sources.title: H.R. 4405 Signed Into Law
sources.relevance: Official White House record confirms presidential signature.

records.text: Kash Patel testified that the FBI had no criminal evidence Epstein trafficked girls to anyone but himself, but documents show Epstein had a worldwide sex-trafficking ring.
records.speaker: Jared Moskowitz

appearances.snippet: Kash Patel under oath said to Senator Kennedy, ... the FBI is not in possession of any criminal evidence that Epstein trafficked girls to anyone but himself. ... We know now that's not true. ... According to documents, ... Epstein had a worldwide sex trafficking ring.

verification.notes: Official testimony confirms Patel said the FBI found no credible, chargeable evidence that Epstein trafficked victims to other people, while DOJ records establish more than 250 victims, multiple locations, and co-conspirator/network evidence. The 'worldwide ring' material does not by itself directly refute Patel's narrower chargeable-evidence formulation.

sources.title: FBI Oversight Hearing Transcript
sources.relevance: Primary transcript records Patel's qualified statement about credible, chargeable evidence.

sources.title: DOJ Releases First Phase of Declassified Epstein Files
sources.relevance: DOJ describes more than 250 victims and Epstein's exploitation network and co-conspirators.

records.text: Ghislaine Maxwell says 29 Epstein associates cut secret Justice Department deals, and six co-conspirator names are available if records are unredacted.
records.speaker: Jared Moskowitz

appearances.snippet: Ghislaine Maxwell says 29 Epstein associates cut secret DOJ deals. ... Six names readily available if you unredact them. Co-conspirators named, ... but we got them when you unredact them.

verification.notes: Maxwell's filed claim, as summarized in an official congressional letter, identifies four named co-conspirators plus 25 men who allegedly received secret settlements and were not indicted. That supports the 29-person arithmetic but overstates the record by describing all 29 as associates who received secret DOJ deals and by merging distinct groups.

sources.title: Rep. Khanna Letter Regarding Maxwell Deposition
sources.relevance: Official congressional letter distinguishes four named co-conspirators from 25 men Maxwell says received secret settlements.

records.text: Jared Moskowitz says Kash Patel's under-oath claim that Donald Trump's name appears fewer than 100 times in the Epstein files is not true.
records.speaker: Jared Moskowitz

appearances.snippet: Kash Patel, under oath, said Trump (Donald Trump)'s name appears less than 100 times in the files. ... We now know that's not true.

verification.notes: The official February 11 hearing transcript confirms Rep. Jared Moskowitz challenged Patel's under-100 figure. Current reporting on the released corpus counted more than 38,000 references across over 5,300 files when related Trump terms were included, so the challenge is well grounded, though many references were duplicates or news material.

sources.title: DOJ Oversight Hearing, February 11, 2026
sources.relevance: Official hearing transcript records Moskowitz's challenge to Patel's under-100 claim.

sources.title: How Often Trump Appears in the Epstein Files
sources.relevance: Reports the broader corpus count of more than 38,000 Trump-related references and explains its scope.

records.text: Howard Lutnick and his family were on Epstein Island in 2012, after Epstein pleaded guilty to state charges.
records.speaker: Jared Moskowitz

appearances.snippet: But now the files are public, ... and in 2012 we found out that he and his family are on Epstein Island. ... after Epstein pled guilty to state charges.

verification.notes: Associated Press reporting based on released records and congressional questioning confirms Howard Lutnick and his family visited Epstein's private island in 2012, after Epstein's 2008 guilty plea.

sources.title: Records show Lutnick and family visited Epstein's island in 2012
sources.relevance: AP reports from released records that Lutnick and his family visited the island in 2012 after Epstein's plea.

records.text: Documents in the Epstein files dispute Donald Trump's claim that he expelled Jeffrey Epstein from his club.
records.speaker: Jared Moskowitz

appearances.snippet: There are documents in the files that dispute the president's claim that he kicked Epstein out of his club.

verification.notes: Current reporting on lawmakers' review of unredacted Epstein records identifies multiple witness accounts—and later an unredacted 2009 attorney email saying Epstein was never asked to leave Mar-a-Lago—that dispute Trump's expulsion account. This verifies the statement that released records dispute the claim.

sources.title: Unredacted Epstein Files Contradict Trump's Mar-a-Lago Claim, Says Lawmaker
sources.relevance: Reports lawmakers' review of witness accounts that dispute Trump's expulsion story.

sources.title: DOJ Oversight Hearing, February 11, 2026
sources.relevance: Primary transcript records the contemporaneous statement that the released records disputed the Mar-a-Lago account.
